FanDuel odds: Buccaneers -8.5, total 41.5
Series History: The Browns won the last meeting between these teams and hold a 7-4 advantage all-time.
Baker Mayfield gets a chance to show the Browns what they're missing after choosing Deshaun Watson over the former No. 1 pick in 2022. Mayfield, who bounced from Carolina to the Rams and then signed with the Buccaneers, said in the offseason this was a game he circled on his calendar. Watson kept the starting job after the Browns fell behind 31-0 at Jacksonville and lost 34-10. Rookie WR Denzel Boston caught a 59-yard touchdown in garbage time, the only highlight in a miserable offensive outing. The Browns struggled to protect Watson, who was sacked five times, lost a fumble and was intercepted. The Buccaneers lost three fumbles, and the costly mistakes tipped the scales in a Week 1 shootout loss to Cincinnati. Mayfield completed 82% of his passes and added a rushing touchdown. RB Bucky Irving contributed 93 scrimmage yards, and WR Emeka Egbuka (five catches, 63 yards) showed strong chemistry with Mayfield. The Browns had little choice but to abandon the running game and Quinshon Judkins. To keep this one tight, they'll need to generate longer drives and keep the vengeful Mayfield on the sideline.
Philadelphia Eagles (1-0) at Tennessee Titans (0-1)
FanDuel odds: Eagles -7, total 39.5
Series History: The Eagles lead the all-time series 8-5.
He heard some boos and then generated the opposite in the opener, but Jalen Hurts threw three touchdowns against the Commanders. RB Saquon Barkley rushed for 83 yards and TE Dallas Goedert delivered two touchdowns as the Eagles kept Washington's defense guessing. The Titans have a few riddles of their own to solve. They lost to the Jets in Week 1 and managed only 195 total yards. Cam Ward averaged only 4.4 yards per pass attempt which clogged lanes near the line of scrimmage in Brian Daboll's first game as offensive coordinator. On the defensive side, Titans LB Anthony Hill was exceptional, posting 16 tackles and two pass breakups. Ward will be responsible for creating big plays to keep pace with Philadelphia. If the Titans can slow Barkley and force Hurts to throw early and often, Tennessee can keep it tight.
Jacksonville Jaguars (1-0) at Denver Broncos (0-1)
Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET
FanDuel odds: Broncos -2.5, total 45.5
Series History: The home team has won four of the past five games in the series, which is tied 7-7 all-time.Jacksonville prepped for a rematch with the Broncos by destroying the Browns 34-10 last week. The Jaguars travel west to face the Broncos in Denver on Sunday. Bo Nix completed 17 of 28 passes for 131 yards, his lowest total since his rookie season in 2024. It certainly didn't help the third-year QB that he was sacked four times and hurried five more times, contributing to converting just 2 of 12 third downs. The Jaguars led the Browns 31-0 after the first drive of the second half before taking their foot off the gas. Trevor Lawrence, who found restored success last season under head coach Liam Coen, had nearly as many touchdown passes (four) as incompletions (five). Lawrence knows it will be tough to find the same success against a Denver defense that finished last season second in yards allowed (278.2 per game) and third in points allowed (18.3). While Denver led the league in sacks (68) a season ago, it managed just two in its loss at Kansas City, while Jacksonville's defense is tied for the league lead with five. That included 1.5 sacks apiece from former first-round picks Travon Walker and Josh Hines-Allen. The Jaguars' receiver room has bumps and bruises. Jacksonville removed Jakobi Meyers (thumb) and Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) from the injury report after they were limited throughout the week in practice.
Las Vegas Raiders (1-0) at Los Angeles Chargers (0-1)
Sunday, 4:05 PM ET
FanDuel odds: Chargers -6.5, total 43.5
Series History: The Chargers have won five of the past six meetings.Pundits are hedging before pushing the chips to the table on a revival in Las Vegas. The Raiders enter Week 2 off an impressive 27-13 win over Miami, but that's the qualifier. The Dolphins are in full-blown rebuilding mode and lack the playmakers to compete with ... almost anyone in the league. The win highlighted the reasons the Raiders opened with Kirk Cousins at quarterback instead of rookie No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza. Cousins was calm and collected, delivered three touchdown passes and spread the ball around. RB Ashton Jeanty took a strong first step toward a rebound season. He collected 147 total yards from scrimmage. Las Vegas' defense had five sacks and held the Dolphins to 74 rushing yards, appropriate to bring up because of the Chargers' run-first approach. The Chargers would like to erase Week 1. LA had 14 points and lost WR Ladd McConkey (ribs) after he scored a touchdown. To open up the running game, offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel wants Herbert to push the ball vertically.
Seattle Seahawks (1-0) at Arizona Cardinals (1-0)
Sunday, 4:25 PM ET
FanDuel odds: Seahawks -4.5, total 41.5
Series History: The Seahawks own nine consecutive wins over the Cardinals.
The Seahawks entrusted the game to their defense for a 13-10 win over New England in the opener after starting QB Sam Darnold left on the opening offensive drive. Drew Lock was efficient in relief, completing 73% of his passes, while Jaxon Smith-Njigba delivered 122 yards and a touchdown. Seattle intercepted three passes and generated consistent pressure. They'll need to get to the pocket quickly this week. Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett threw to his primary or first read on almost every pass last week. For the Seahawks, getting rookie Jadarian Price will be a focus. He'll be opposite his former Notre Dame backfield teammate Jeremiyah Love, who had a strong debut to help Arizona surprise the Chargers.
Washington Commanders (0-1) at Dallas Cowboys (0-1)
FanDuel odds: Cowboys -4.5, total 50.5
Series History: The Cowboys have won five of the past six meetings in the series.
Dak Prescott has only two career losses to the Commanders and is chasing redemption with WRs George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb after a Week 1 defeat. Commanders QB Jayden Daniels was inconsistent in Week 1, but came alive late to make things interesting at Philadelphia thanks to rookie wideout Antonio Williams. He was a bright spot with 64 yards and a touchdown and all four receptions were long enough to move the chains. RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt has big-play speed and had two touchdowns in the last meeting with the Cowboys in December. The Cowboys might look to work underneath and between the hashmarks as the Eagles had great success working the ball to TE Dallas Goedert last week. Dallas lost a close game to the Giants, allowing 394 yards and struggling against the run. Rookie Caleb Downs was impressive with a sack and forced fumble but the Cowboys are banged up in the secondary already. OLB Donovan Ezeiruaku brought pressure off the edge, but the Giants converted 9 of 11 third-down tries and had too much time to survey the field. Protecting Daniels against Dallas' aggressive pass rush could decide momentum early in the game. Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker didn't have a dream of an opener in the loss at New York but he trained under Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio.
Miami Dolphins (0-1) at San Francisco 49ers (1-0)
FanDuel odds: 49ers -13.5, total 45.5
Series History: The Dolphins won the last meeting (29-17) in 2024. 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan is 1-2 against Miami.QB Malik Willis threw for 220 yards but the Miami offense struggled to finish drives in the Week 1 loss at Las Vegas. Willis had two rookie receivers in the starting lineup. Caleb Douglas was a bright spot with 94 yards. RB De'Von Achane added 66 total yards and is the player the 49ers -- and most opponents -- will game plan to stop. The Dolphins have to put up points to keep pace with a diverse and balanced 49ers scheme with Brock Purdy at the controls. While the Dolphins forced two turnovers at Las Vegas, the Miami run defense allowed 130 yards, and top pass rusher Chop Robinson (concussion) is out this week. San Francisco opened its season with a dominant 27-7 thrashing of the Rams in Australia. The offensive line was a major advantage in the game and it stands out as a mismatch against Miami. RB Christian McCaffrey could be in line for a massive game. He had 146 total yards in his last game against the Dolphins.
Indianapolis Colts (0-1) at Kansas City Chiefs (1-0)
Sunday, 8:20 p.m. ET
FanDuel odds: Chiefs -6.5, total 46.5
Series History: The Chiefs beat the Colts 23-20 in overtime last season, breaking a two-game losing streak in the series.
Indy's beleaguered defense has already swapped its lead 'blue-dot' communicator on defense, from S Cam Bynum to LB Akeem Davis-Gaither. The Colts are overturning every stone to try to figure out how the opener against the Ravens went so poorly. A run defense whipped by Derrick Henry and Lamar Jackson (202 yards, four TDs) is praying that Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker III won't have much left for an encore in KC. Walker had 173 rushing yards and 18 receiving yards on three catches to power the Chiefs to a Monday night victory over the Broncos. Colts RB Jonathan Taylor did his part in the opener, with the exception of a rare fumble. He had 98 yards and two TDs. But QB Daniel Jones couldn't get the passing game to fire. WR Alec Pierce had four receptions but Indianapolis amassed only 251 total yards. Pierce (heel) has been bothered by the same injury that limited him in the offseason, but he's a go for Sunday night after being removed from the injury report.

The Saints went for two and the upset victory of Detroit in overtime in a one-point loss, but their offense came away looking like a winner. QB Tyler Shough's 410-yard, three-touchdown performance generated plenty of excitement around the young quarterback. WR Chris Olave had 182 receiving yards and New Orleans held up reasonably well in pass protection but did allow five sacks. Still, Shough was able to take consistent shots downfield. The Ravens overwhelmed Indianapolis in Week 1, generating turnovers and consistent pressure on Daniel Jones. Baltimore also put on an offensive show at Indy. QB Lamar Jackson appeared to have quickly mastered new play-caller Declan Doyle's scheme. Jackson threw for 324 yards and added a rushing touchdown, while Derrick Henry delivered a vintage performance with 144 rushing yards and three scores. Where Jackson will go with the ball on pass plays will depend on whether WR Zay Flowers (hamstring) is back in the lineup. Flowers posted a career-high 150 yards in Week 1 without playing a snap in the second half.
Minnesota Vikings (1-0) at Chicago Bears (1-0)
FanDuel odds: Bears -4.5, total 47.5
Series History: In the 2020s, the Vikings are 9-3 in this matchup. They swept the season series in 2021, 2022 and 2024.
Rain and wind could become a factor Sunday as the Vikings venture outside the dome for a second consecutive division matchup. Minnesota opened the season with a 39-22 win over Green Bay despite losing Kyler Murray (concussion) in the first half. Carson Wentz led the rally with four consecutive TD drives in the second half. Wentz had three touchdown passes and leaned heavily on WR Justin Jefferson, who finished with 92 yards and two scores. The Vikings did allow nearly 400 passing yards as they lived and died with the blitz, firing five-plus defenders into the pocket on more than 65 percent of their snaps. There will be a risk-reward balance at Chicago. The Bears put up 59 points with a dominant ground game producing six touchdowns. QB Caleb Williams said he's looking forward to the cat-and-mouse game with Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores. Williams had 269 yards and two touchdowns through the air and added two rushing TDs. D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai combined for 224 rushing yards. The Bears did not throw a perfect game defensively at Carolina and getting pressure on Wentz will be of significant importance.
Cincinnati Bengals (1-0) at Houston Texans (0-1)
FanDuel odds: Texans -2.5, total 45.5
Series History: The Texans have won four of the past five meetings.
Joe Burrow completed 71% of his passes and the Bengals generated 351 total yards against the Buccaneers, but they had their defense -- and three forced fumbles -- to thank for coming out on top. The Bengals had four sacks and four takeaways. They shift their focus to C.J. Stroud, who won't have No. 1 WR Nico Collins (hamstring) available. Stroud threw for 274 yards and two touchdowns in Week 1 while RB David Montgomery carried the offense with three TDs. The Texans can get to Burrow, but the issue last week was communication in the back seven. Houston was hammered by Josh Allen and the Bills for 409 total yards. With Collins out, the Bengals can tip the scales in their favor by handling Montgomery.
Pittsburgh Steelers (1-0) at New England Patriots (0-1)
FanDuel odds: Patriots -4.5, total 41.5
Series History: The Steelers lead 16-15; the Patriots have won three of the last four.
The Steelers let their defense do the dirty work in Week 1. LBs T.J. Watt and Alex Highsmith combined for four sacks, Watt had a pick-6 and the Falcons leaned almost entirely on RB Bijan Robinson for offense. The Patriots welcome back RB TreVeyon Henderson after he sat out Week 1 with an ankle injury. He brings a valuable speed and big-play threat, and QB Drake Maye could use a crutch after his three-INT opener at Seattle. Maye also lost No. 1 WR A.J. Brown (ankle) in the loss and Romeo Doubs didn't make a great first impression with costly drops. Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers (221 yards, one passing TD), back in Mike McCarthy's scheme, worked from the middle of the field to the sideline last week.
Green Bay Packers (0-1) at New York Jets (1-0)
FanDuel odds: Packers -3.5, total 44.5
Series History: The Packers have won three of the past four meetings.
There could be changes afoot on the Packers' offensive line. QB Jordan Love threw for 387 yards in a loss to the Vikings but felt pressure consistently. It might be too soon for major changes on defense, but coordinator Jonathon Gannon admitted this week Green Bay won't win games surrendering 39 points. WR Christian Watson looked the part as Love's go-to guy. He worked in the slot often, where his size and speed make him a nightmare for most defenses. Watson finished with 147 yards and two touchdowns. Second-year pro Matthew Golden added 95 receiving yards. The Packers are still searching for a rotation they can trust at running back with Josh Jacobs on the exempt list. The Jets opened their season with a convincing 23-10 win over Tennessee, highlighted by a balanced offensive attack and strong defensive play. Geno Smith was aggressive and efficient, completing nearly 80% of his passes. RB Breece Hall likely has Gannon concerned after he dominated with 118 total yards.
Cleveland Browns (0-1) at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (0-1)
FanDuel odds: Buccaneers -8.5, total 41.5
Series History: The Browns won the last meeting between these teams and hold a 7-4 advantage all-time.
Baker Mayfield gets a chance to show the Browns what they're missing after choosing Deshaun Watson over the former No. 1 pick in 2022. Mayfield, who bounced from Carolina to the Rams and then signed with the Buccaneers, said in the offseason this was a game he circled on his calendar. Watson kept the starting job after the Browns fell behind 31-0 at Jacksonville and lost 34-10. Rookie WR Denzel Boston caught a 59-yard touchdown in garbage time, the only highlight in a miserable offensive outing. The Browns struggled to protect Watson, who was sacked five times, lost a fumble and was intercepted. The Buccaneers lost three fumbles, and the costly mistakes tipped the scales in a Week 1 shootout loss to Cincinnati. Mayfield completed 82% of his passes and added a rushing touchdown. RB Bucky Irving contributed 93 scrimmage yards, and WR Emeka Egbuka (five catches, 63 yards) showed strong chemistry with Mayfield. The Browns had little choice but to abandon the running game and Quinshon Judkins. To keep this one tight, they'll need to generate longer drives and keep the vengeful Mayfield on the sideline.
Philadelphia Eagles (1-0) at Tennessee Titans (0-1)
FanDuel odds: Eagles -7, total 39.5
Series History: The Eagles lead the all-time series 8-5.
He heard some boos and then generated the opposite in the opener, but Jalen Hurts threw three touchdowns against the Commanders. RB Saquon Barkley rushed for 83 yards and TE Dallas Goedert delivered two touchdowns as the Eagles kept Washington's defense guessing. The Titans have a few riddles of their own to solve. They lost to the Jets in Week 1 and managed only 195 total yards. Cam Ward averaged only 4.4 yards per pass attempt which clogged lanes near the line of scrimmage in Brian Daboll's first game as offensive coordinator. On the defensive side, Titans LB Anthony Hill was exceptional, posting 16 tackles and two pass breakups. Ward will be responsible for creating big plays to keep pace with Philadelphia. If the Titans can slow Barkley and force Hurts to throw early and often, Tennessee can keep it tight.
Jacksonville Jaguars (1-0) at Denver Broncos (0-1)
Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET
FanDuel odds: Broncos -2.5, total 45.5
Series History: The home team has won four of the past five games in the series, which is tied 7-7 all-time.Jacksonville prepped for a rematch with the Broncos by destroying the Browns 34-10 last week. The Jaguars travel west to face the Broncos in Denver on Sunday. Bo Nix completed 17 of 28 passes for 131 yards, his lowest total since his rookie season in 2024. It certainly didn't help the third-year QB that he was sacked four times and hurried five more times, contributing to converting just 2 of 12 third downs. The Jaguars led the Browns 31-0 after the first drive of the second half before taking their foot off the gas. Trevor Lawrence, who found restored success last season under head coach Liam Coen, had nearly as many touchdown passes (four) as incompletions (five). Lawrence knows it will be tough to find the same success against a Denver defense that finished last season second in yards allowed (278.2 per game) and third in points allowed (18.3). While Denver led the league in sacks (68) a season ago, it managed just two in its loss at Kansas City, while Jacksonville's defense is tied for the league lead with five. That included 1.5 sacks apiece from former first-round picks Travon Walker and Josh Hines-Allen. The Jaguars' receiver room has bumps and bruises. Jacksonville removed Jakobi Meyers (thumb) and Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) from the injury report after they were limited throughout the week in practice.
Las Vegas Raiders (1-0) at Los Angeles Chargers (0-1)
Sunday, 4:05 PM ET
FanDuel odds: Chargers -6.5, total 43.5
Series History: The Chargers have won five of the past six meetings.Pundits are hedging before pushing the chips to the table on a revival in Las Vegas. The Raiders enter Week 2 off an impressive 27-13 win over Miami, but that's the qualifier. The Dolphins are in full-blown rebuilding mode and lack the playmakers to compete with ... almost anyone in the league. The win highlighted the reasons the Raiders opened with Kirk Cousins at quarterback instead of rookie No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza. Cousins was calm and collected, delivered three touchdown passes and spread the ball around. RB Ashton Jeanty took a strong first step toward a rebound season. He collected 147 total yards from scrimmage. Las Vegas' defense had five sacks and held the Dolphins to 74 rushing yards, appropriate to bring up because of the Chargers' run-first approach. The Chargers would like to erase Week 1. LA had 14 points and lost WR Ladd McConkey (ribs) after he scored a touchdown. To open up the running game, offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel wants Herbert to push the ball vertically.
Seattle Seahawks (1-0) at Arizona Cardinals (1-0)
Sunday, 4:25 PM ET
FanDuel odds: Seahawks -4.5, total 41.5
Series History: The Seahawks own nine consecutive wins over the Cardinals.
The Seahawks entrusted the game to their defense for a 13-10 win over New England in the opener after starting QB Sam Darnold left on the opening offensive drive. Drew Lock was efficient in relief, completing 73% of his passes, while Jaxon Smith-Njigba delivered 122 yards and a touchdown. Seattle intercepted three passes and generated consistent pressure. They'll need to get to the pocket quickly this week. Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett threw to his primary or first read on almost every pass last week. For the Seahawks, getting rookie Jadarian Price will be a focus. He'll be opposite his former Notre Dame backfield teammate Jeremiyah Love, who had a strong debut to help Arizona surprise the Chargers.
Washington Commanders (0-1) at Dallas Cowboys (0-1)
FanDuel odds: Cowboys -4.5, total 50.5
Series History: The Cowboys have won five of the past six meetings in the series.
Dak Prescott has only two career losses to the Commanders and is chasing redemption with WRs George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb after a Week 1 defeat. Commanders QB Jayden Daniels was inconsistent in Week 1, but came alive late to make things interesting at Philadelphia thanks to rookie wideout Antonio Williams. He was a bright spot with 64 yards and a touchdown and all four receptions were long enough to move the chains. RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt has big-play speed and had two touchdowns in the last meeting with the Cowboys in December. The Cowboys might look to work underneath and between the hashmarks as the Eagles had great success working the ball to TE Dallas Goedert last week. Dallas lost a close game to the Giants, allowing 394 yards and struggling against the run. Rookie Caleb Downs was impressive with a sack and forced fumble but the Cowboys are banged up in the secondary already. OLB Donovan Ezeiruaku brought pressure off the edge, but the Giants converted 9 of 11 third-down tries and had too much time to survey the field. Protecting Daniels against Dallas' aggressive pass rush could decide momentum early in the game. Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker didn't have a dream of an opener in the loss at New York but he trained under Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio.
Miami Dolphins (0-1) at San Francisco 49ers (1-0)
FanDuel odds: 49ers -13.5, total 45.5
Series History: The Dolphins won the last meeting (29-17) in 2024. 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan is 1-2 against Miami.QB Malik Willis threw for 220 yards but the Miami offense struggled to finish drives in the Week 1 loss at Las Vegas. Willis had two rookie receivers in the starting lineup. Caleb Douglas was a bright spot with 94 yards. RB De'Von Achane added 66 total yards and is the player the 49ers -- and most opponents -- will game plan to stop. The Dolphins have to put up points to keep pace with a diverse and balanced 49ers scheme with Brock Purdy at the controls. While the Dolphins forced two turnovers at Las Vegas, the Miami run defense allowed 130 yards, and top pass rusher Chop Robinson (concussion) is out this week. San Francisco opened its season with a dominant 27-7 thrashing of the Rams in Australia. The offensive line was a major advantage in the game and it stands out as a mismatch against Miami. RB Christian McCaffrey could be in line for a massive game. He had 146 total yards in his last game against the Dolphins.
Indianapolis Colts (0-1) at Kansas City Chiefs (1-0)
Sunday, 8:20 p.m. ET
FanDuel odds: Chiefs -6.5, total 46.5
Series History: The Chiefs beat the Colts 23-20 in overtime last season, breaking a two-game losing streak in the series.
Indy's beleaguered defense has already swapped its lead 'blue-dot' communicator on defense, from S Cam Bynum to LB Akeem Davis-Gaither. The Colts are overturning every stone to try to figure out how the opener against the Ravens went so poorly. A run defense whipped by Derrick Henry and Lamar Jackson (202 yards, four TDs) is praying that Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker III won't have much left for an encore in KC. Walker had 173 rushing yards and 18 receiving yards on three catches to power the Chiefs to a Monday night victory over the Broncos. Colts RB Jonathan Taylor did his part in the opener, with the exception of a rare fumble. He had 98 yards and two TDs. But QB Daniel Jones couldn't get the passing game to fire. WR Alec Pierce had four receptions but Indianapolis amassed only 251 total yards. Pierce (heel) has been bothered by the same injury that limited him in the offseason, but he's a go for Sunday night after being removed from the injury report.

Title: Rise Against and Alkaline Trio Swap Songs for New Split Record Ahead of Joint Tour
Article_Text:
Rise Against and Alkaline Trio are heading out on a big joint tour this fall. To kick things off, the pair have dropped a split record where they each cover a song by the other.
On the new 2-song project, Rise Against takes on Alkaline Trio’s “Private Eye.” Then, Alkaline Trio delivers their rendition of Rise Against’s “Re-Education (Through Labor).” I know I’m aging myself here, but it’s essentially an elder-Millennial punk rock kids’ dream collab.
Videos by VICE
In a press release statement, Rise Against’s Tim McIlrath noted how the Chicago-punk mutuals have a history that supersedes even their own individual careers.
“The connection between Alkaline Trio and Rise Against actually pre-dates both bands’ inceptions,” he said. “So we’ve all been there for both the awkward first steps and the flashes of promise. We have an understanding and appreciation of each other’s bands that could only come from being from the same scene.”
McIlrath added, “To still be standing this many years later is a testament to the fertile Chicago musical soil we come from and are proud to represent. We had so much fun sinking our teeth into their legendary song ‘Private Eye’.”
Rise Against and Alkaline Trio both came up in the late 90s Chicago punk scene
Alkaline Trio frontman Matt Skiba spoke on the project as well, saying it’s a full-circle moment, two decades in the making. “It’s so much fun and such an honor to be swapping cover tunes with a band we’ve known personally and loved since we both formed and came up from our shows at the Fireside Bowl in Chicago,” shared Skiba.
He continued, “To see Rise Against become the band they are today has been a blast to track and to be a small part of through the years. To reconnect with this band and these people once again the way we are via tour, and this release feels the way it did when we first started: it’s almost completely for the love of each other and each other’s band. It feels like a tradition we started decades ago that naturally comes back to us; we are grateful to say.”

Title: Joel Embiid trade could actually help set the Clippers' future straight
Article_Text:
Don't roll your eyes yet, if you haven't already. This isn't the kind of headline you wanted to read as an LA Clippers fan, but it's the reality. After losing five first-round picks as one of the penalties in the cap-circumvention scandal, Joel Embiid could help the team recoup some of those assets.
Yossi Gozlan and Sam Quinn discussed whether the Clippers will become a dumping ground for bad contracts on the "Third Apron Podcast," specifically naming Embiid because the three-year extension he signed with the Sixers, which kicks in this season, doesn't look all that good.
"Are you willing and able to take damaged goods? Somebody who's injured, somebody who's older, somebody who has a contract that doesn't really fit into the structure of whatever their team is building. Joel Embiid is a really obvious one."
Philadelphia isn't ready to send Embiid packing, at least not yet. The Sixers entered the offseason needing to find a way to trade him or Paul George, and they managed to send the forward to the Celtics for Jaylen Brown, but that doesn't mean the star center will remain in Philly.
Embiid is on the most talented team he's been on since the Sixers drafted him in 2014, and while that will play in his favor by taking some of the pressure off him, at least in the regular season, that pressure will ramp up in the playoffs.
What if Philadelphia decides that trading Embiid is necessary to maximize its chances of winning a title? Should LA come calling? Yes, actually.
Clippers can get draft assets in Joel Embiid trade
The two unprotected first-round picks and two first-round pick swaps LA received from Toronto in the Kawhi Leonard trade have already helped put the Clippers on the right path. But that doesn't change the fact that the team has its work cut out for it.
The next few years will be rough, and while the anti-tanking reform the NBA put in place this season won't reward finishing at the bottom of the standings, LA has little choice but to take that route because of the position it put itself in.
Embiid will make a little less than $58 million this season, $62.6 million in 2027-28, and has a $62.3 million player option in 2028-29 that you can already assume he will exercise. If Philly decides it's best to trade him before the February deadline, or even next summer, that contract will be a hard sell unless you're LA.
The Clippers could try to get back the 2028 pick the Sixers sent in the 2023 James Harden trade, which looks much better now than it did then because of the Kawhi scandal. Philadelphia should want to hold onto it for that reason, but getting off Embiid's contract would justify parting ways with it. And it would take more than that to make a deal happen, but that'd be a great start.
Acquiring Embiid would be a key piece of the puzzle for LA in building a future that can actually give fans something to look forward to. Still, to get there, Philadelphia will have to conclude that it's time to close that chapter with the former No. 1 pick and NBA MVP. Given his struggles to stay healthy and on the floor, the Clippers should be ready for that.

Title: Eagles' final Week 2 injury report: Jonathan Greenard out once again
Article_Text:
Philadelphia Eagles fans were hoping for some good injury news rolling into the weekend, but it appears the team will be without edge rusher Jonathan Greenard for the second straight week.
The Eagles have announced their final injury report for their Week 2 matchup against the Tennessee Titans. Greenard is the only player who is listed as out with a pectoral injury.
Before training camp, Greenard injured his pectoral while working out in the weight room. He ended up missing all of training camp and has been limited in practice throughout the last two weeks.
Impact of Jonathan Greenard being out for Eagles in Week 2
The Eagles will at least have Nolan Smith and Jalyx Hunt to handle things. Those two have plenty of experience being in the starting lineup throughout the last two season.
Hunt had a great opening game in the 24-22 win over the Washington Commanders, racking up seven pressures. Philly will need more of that from their young edge rusher.
Smith has been decent, but isn't making the highlight plays the Eagles need him to be for a former first-round pick. This is a critical game for Smith to really cement himself in the lineup because if Greenard returns next week, Hunt would have to be the choice.
Andrew Mukuba listed as questionable for the Titans game for Eagles
Starting safety Mukuba is the other Eagles player with an injury status, as he was listed as questionable with knee injury. He was seen leaving a sleeve on it after Thursday's practice, which he did not participate in. Mukuba seemed to indicate to reporters that he will play.
He is coming off a solid Week 1 game against the Commanders, as his coverage skills are improving. Mukuba is seen as a key player at safety, being a younger player with a ton of upside.
If Mukuba can't play in the game, it could be Marcus Epps and Michael Carter in the game. That wouldn't be the worst thing in the world, but Mukuba makes this secondary good.
Eagles will have Cooper DeJean and Jalen Carter in Week 2 game
DeJean and Carter missed part of the week with their own injuries. Carter is dealing with a wrist injury, but was seen in a cast. DeJean is dealing with a calf/abdomen injury.
Both guys have no injury status, which means they should be good to play in the Titans game. These are difference-makers that fans will be happy to have on the field.

Title: Eagles' underrated safety unit has answered the call through one game
Article_Text:
For a position group under the microscope since veteran Reed Blankenship's departure, the Philadelphia Eagles' safety group ignored the outside noise this summer, stacking solid practices as they worked to prove the doubters wrong.
In Week 1's 24-22 win over Washington, Marcus Epps and Andrew Mukuba delivered a strong showing that quelled critics, with the new starting duo displaying efficiency, awareness, and toughness.
With the star power possessed by the current Philadelphia cornerback group, an efficient performance is more important than ever in the safety unit. A weak link can, and absolutely will, be exposed by the opposition, but in Week 1 action, Marcus Epps and Andrew Mukuba absolutely answered the call.
Eagles' safety position is looking to be in solid position entering Week 2
The tandem didn't allow a big play on their watch, and while the veteran Epps provided his usual tenacity with seven tackles, Mukuba, now in his second season, looked decidedly improved in his play recognition and overall awareness.
In total, they combined to surrender just two catches for 14 yards, a solid first showing patrolling the secondary together.
Fresh off their promising regular-season debut, Andrew Mukuba and Marcus Epps will look to keep building in Week 2's trip to Music City to face the Tennessee Titans.
Titans can't be slept on at skill positions by Eagles' Marcus Epps and Andrew Mukuba
In Tennessee's Week 1 loss to the New York Jets, the Titans' pass protection flaws surfaced time and again. Quarterback Cam Ward was repeatedly forced out of his comfort zone, fleeing the pocket in hopes of keeping plays alive. Expect the Eagles' pass rush to post pressures, hurries, and sacks in this Week 2 tilt, forcing Ward to look for early throws to get rid of the ball under consistent duress.
And while the timing and pass protection could be shaky for the home team again in Week 2, the Eagles' secondary must help blanket a cast of skill-position players who can do damage if found open. Prized first-rounder Carnell Tate out of Ohio State will align outside for the corners to tango with, while weapons such as Wandale Robinson and tight end Gunnar Helm will venture plenty over the middle where Mukuba and Epps mainly operate. Coming out of the backfield, Tony Pollard can make plays in the passing phase as well, so he'll also be firmly on the radar for the safety duo.
Eagles fans know Robinson well from his four seasons withseasons with Big Blue, and Helm is a developing second-year tight end out of the University of Texas who can make plays. The group has upside, but overall, it's not a potent cast of playmakers. After facing the likes of Terry McClaurin, Stefon Diggs, and rookie Antonio Williams in Week 1, the Philly secondary enters Week 2 ready to shut this opposing offense down.
Eagles safeties could have loud weekend in Music City
This Titans offense is highly susceptible to turnovers, given its shaky offensive line and a quarterback who still has much to prove at the pro level. A strong pass rush will force Ward to scramble for daylight, and forced throws into tight windows could be in store.
This is a great spot for a pick by Mukuba (two interceptions in 2025), or perhaps a forced fumble by the hard-hitting Epps this weekend.

It's only just begun, but the season is off to a strong start for this new safety duo. Epps and Mukuba are out to prove they can hold down the fort at safety long-term, and you can count on them being fully prepared for the Week 2 mission at hand.

Title: David Blough can exploit Cowboys with Commanders trick barely seen on tape
Article_Text:
David Blough's offense was a mixed bag in Week 1 of his tenure as offensive coordinator. The Washington Commanders started slowly but finished strong against the Philadelphia Eagles. The first-time NFL play-caller also has one trick left up his sleeve that he didn't use nearly enough at Lincoln Financial Field.
Everyone knows how the Dallas Cowboys linebacker unit struggled against the New York Giants on Sunday Night Football. They were abysmal from start to finish, and DeMarvion Overshown is once again dealing with injury problems, which only raises concerns.
The Commanders can take advantage of this. And it should all start with Blough calling more play-action shots at AT&T Stadium.
Commanders must unleash more play-action against the suspect Cowboys defense
Blough didn't deploy much play-action in Philadelphia. Perhaps the offensive coordinator was wary about the Eagles generating pressure with just four defensive linemen, which is fair. But the Cowboys aren't as strong, so a little more creativity could provide the spark they need.
And it might be a surprise the Cowboys don't see coming.
The Commanders still have the element of surprise in their favor, which is rare between these two bitter division rivals. Blough has called only one game, and there is no way he's unleashed his full bag of nuances yet. With the stakes this high, there's never been a better time to do just that.
First, the Commanders must establish the run. They have the options to make things difficult, but the offensive line must help more. They won't be going up against Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis, but they do have the supreme threat of Quinnen Williams to counteract.
Difficult, but not impossible.
Play-action can unlock a different side of Commanders' offense in Dallas
If the trenches are secure and the ground game keeps the Cowboys' defense guessing, play-action will be critical. Teams always have to account for quarterback Jayden Daniels' rushing ability, and Dallas' second level will show some extra hesitancy that could be exploited.
They also have the wide receiver to make this happen. Terry McLaurin, Stefon Diggs, and Antonio Williams wouldn't be classed as burners by any stretch, but they recognize soft spots in coverage and are prolific in one-on-one matchups. If the Cowboys are forced to stack the box, that will open things up considerably.
And, of course, Daniels' deep-ball prowess is renowned and respected in equal measure.
Before eating, you have to lay the table. Washington's ground game will be tasked with this responsibility. If they get early success, play-action will inevitably become a factor.
Daniels is now more comfortable playing under center, too. It's one of the primary reasons why Kliff Kingsbury was removed, and Blough was installed. There would be no better time to show it than in Dallas as the Commanders look to avoid going 0-2 on the year.
Let's see if all the pieces come together.

Title: Goodwalkspoiled Set To Take Her Swing
Article_Text:
Goodwalkspoiled is ready to tee it up in the Kentucky Championship.
A two-year-old daughter of Pebble Beach whose name is a nod to the oft-quoted description of playing golf, Goodwalkspoiled will be among nine horses hoping to capture the trophy in Sunday’s (Sept. 20) $400,000 USD Kentucky Championship Series final for freshman filly pacers at The Red Mile.
The Red Mile hosts all eight Kentucky Championship Series finals for pacers and trotters on Sunday, with racing beginning at 5:05 p.m. (EDT). The Kentucky Championship events are races three through 10.
Goodwalkspoiled has posted three wins in five races this season and earned $97,049 for driver Kyle Husted and trainer Amy Husted, with Husted Racing LLC sharing ownership of the filly with John Schwarz Jr. She won a leg of the Kentucky Championship Series on Aug. 25 in 1:51 at the Red Mile. On Aug. 4, she won a division of the lower-level Commonwealth Series in 1:50, a mark that is the fastest of the Championship Series finalists and ranks behind only three two-year-old filly pacers in North America.
She will leave from post seven on Sunday and is the 9-2 third choice on the morning line.
“We’ve known since training her down that she was wicked fast,” Amy Husted said. “She was a little tricky to get going – she had some attitude issues – but once it clicked, we knew she had the speed. Around March, we knew she was pretty nice. But you could have a nice one, and then everyone else has a lot nicer ones. So, you never know. We didn’t want to get our hopes up. But we knew she was special; for us, anyway.
“I like her spunkiness,” Amy added. “She’s very nice to jog and train, she’s smart, and she takes care of herself – but she has feistiness to her as well.”
Goodwalkspoiled, out of the mare Play Nice, is from the first crop of stallion Pebble Beach, who was a Dan Patch Award winner as a three-year-old in 2022. The Indiana-based Husteds purchased Goodwalkspoiled, a half-sister to Pennsylvania stakes winner Aintplayinnice, for $38,028 at this past October’s Midwest Standardbred Select Yearling Sale.
“We loved watching Pebble Beach race, and Kyle and I always said we thought he would be a really good sire because he was so fast,” Amy said. “We looked at her at the sale, and we fell in love with her. She was big, strong, perfect conformation. We thought she would be out of our price range. Maybe we just got lucky.”
Goodwalkspoiled heads to Sunday’s race off a seventh-place Championship Series finish on Sept. 6, when she led for three-quarters of the race. Her past four starts show a pattern of alternating wins and seventh-place finishes.
“She wins and then she throws a clunker,” Amy said. “Last week, was her clunker. Maybe this will be her good week.”
Amy added about the performances, “The times that she raced below average, she scoped with some mucous. Not anything terrible, just a little sickness. When you have to race as tough as these races, you have to be a hundred per cent. We’ve battled a lot of allergy issues with her all year, and I think that just got the best of her.”
Sunday’s $400,000 USD purse will equal the most lucrative that Husted’s training stable has competed for.
“It’s what we dream about,” Amy said. “Especially with one that we picked out, and broke and trained down. Our partner is great. We’ve had horses together going on six years now, and he’s amazing and very supportive. It would be just so much fun if we could get a little piece of it. It’s definitely what we’ve dreamt about for a long time.”
Kountry Legacy, a daughter of Capt Midnight-Shartin N, is the 5-2 morning-line favourite in the Kentucky Championship Series final for two-year-old filly pacers. She has four wins and two second-place finishes in seven races this season. She will leave from post three with Trace Tetrick driving for trainer Jeff Cullipher.
The 7-2 second choice is My Taylors Swift, who has a win and four seconds in six races. She will go from post six with Ronnie Wrenn Jr. in the sulky for trainer Ron Burke.

Title: Trump says some routine immunizations will be split into five separate shots. Vaccine experts say it won't work
Article_Text:
President Donald Trump said Friday that his administration is planning to recommend that certain childhood immunizations be broken up into five separate shots, each with a “small amount of the vaccine.” These “20% doses” would each be given six months apart, he said.
“Instead of a child going in and having a tremendous amount of different vaccines pumped into a big proportion of the body … we’re going to recommend that they do five doses marked one, two, three, four, five and that they be given in six-month intervals, so that a small amount of the vaccine gets pumped into the body,” Trump said.
Such a plan would render vaccines ineffective and wouldn’t make them safer, said Dr. Paul Offit, director of the Vaccine Education Center at the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia.
Trump also said Friday that “certain vaccines were taken out because they’re not needed until the child would be much older,” an apparent reference to the federal childhood vaccine schedule — which the administration attempted to overhaul this year before it was temporarily blocked by a federal judge.
It’s unclear which vaccines Trump was referring to at Friday’s news conference; he specifically mentioned only the polio vaccine, which he said has “been amazing.”
Trump suggested that the federal vaccination schedule changes he referenced Friday would lead to a “massive reduction in autism,” even though extensive scientific studies of vaccines have yielded no evidence of a connection to autism.
The US Department of Health and Human Services has not responded to CNN’s request for further details about the plans that Trump outlined Friday.
HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. — who was standing by Trump as he outlined the planned vaccine changes — received a standing ovation Thursday at the conference of the anti-vaccine advocacy group Children’s Health Defense, where he gave the keynote. He praised Trump’s embrace of vaccine skeptics, telling the conference attendees, “you have a strong and steadfast friend at the White House” and saying he would “stay in this fight.”
In August, Trump signed an executive order aimed at reshaping the federal government’s approach toward childhood vaccines, insisting that infants should receive fewer immunizations over a longer period and advising that the measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccine be separated into three individual shots, despite little scientific evidence supporting such sweeping changes.
Trump has previously claimed that “large amounts – like vats of vaccine – are currently pumped into your child’s body” and that this supposedly large volume of fluid – “the size of a bottle of soda” – was dangerous.
The standard dose of MMR vaccine given to children around 12 months of age is 0.5 milliliters, or CCs, about one-tenth of a teaspoon.
Trump’s idea to split up the shots “is buffoonery,” said Offit, a vaccine inventor. He noted that vaccines are studied extensively so their dosing schedule is optimized for efficacy and safety, and he said that reducing the amount administered and giving more shots would make it so the vaccines don’t work while doing nothing to increase safety.
“When you create a vaccine, you do a dose response curve, and you’re trying to give the least amount of vaccine that induces an immune response that’s protective. So you don’t want to give too much, where you know you don’t need all that, and you don’t want to give too little, where it’s you know sub-immunogenic,” meaning it wouldn’t induce an immune response. Put more simply, Offit told CNN, “What he’s suggesting would not work. He’s basically saying he wants to give vaccines in a manner in which they wouldn’t be protective.”
            Offit also pointed out that vaccines don’t overwhelm babies’ immune systems, as they expose us to much less than we encounter every day naturally. 
“You make a billion new B and T cells every day to handle the onslaught of viruses and bacteria from your environment,” Offit said. “Vaccines are literally a drop in the ocean of what you encounter and manage every day.
“The notion that vaccines in any way are overwhelming your immune system, causing chronic disease, is just fanciful.”
    
CNN’s Tami Luhby, Brenda Goodman and Jen Christensen contributed to this report.

Title: Locked Out: Should You Take 'Free Money' to Buy a Home? | National
Article_Text:
If you’re stretching toward a home purchase, anything that shrinks the pile of cash you need at closing looks pretty appealing.
Homebuying assistance programs — usually in the form of help with your down payment or closing costs — could mean affording to buy now instead of waiting. Jeffrey Ruben, president of WSFS Home Lending in Greater Philadelphia, estimates about 12% of closings at WSFS Bank rely on some type of homebuying assistance.
“Clearly a minority of the borrowing public is taking advantage of this, or has the ability to take advantage of it,” he says.
Eligible buyers receive an average benefit of $18,000, according to Down Payment Resource, which tracks homebuying assistance programs. But qualifications can be strict, and funds can come with strings.
“Locked Out” is a series about why buying a home feels out of reach, and the solutions that could change the game. This time, I’m looking at who offers down payment assistance, when it pays off and what buyers should know before saying yes.
Not all programs are created equal
When researching your options, start close to home. State and local governments offer more than half of all homebuying assistance programs, according to Down Payment Resource. Nonprofits, like the Neighborhood Assistance Program of America and niche regional programs, run another 22%.
First-time buyers with lower income have the most choices for down payment assistance, but repeat buyers and higher earners shouldn’t count themselves out. About one in 10 programs don’t have income limits, reports Down Payment Resource.
Ruben says government-backed programs are typically the best options because they’re designed with a public goal in mind, such as revitalizing a neighborhood or expanding homeownership. Home builders also offer buyer credits or discounts, but there’s usually something in it for them — like directing buyers to their in-house financing.
“If it's coming from the guy who's trying to sell you the house, you know, you have to really kind of be skeptical of that,” Ruben says.
You might have more choices than you think, but look beyond the dollar amount. Consider who’s offering the help and whether the details work for you.
Does the program fit your future plans?
Consider how the assistance itself is structured. It may be a grant, tax credit, forgivable loan or loan you’ll eventually repay. Each one has trade-offs that might not be strictly financial.
“It can turn into, quote-unquote, 'free money,’” Ruben says. “But there's a cost.”
For example, some programs structure assistance as a second mortgage. You may or may not owe monthly payments, but the debt can limit your ability to sell, refinance or rent out the home. A forgivable loan might require you to stay in the home for five or 10 years. Move sooner, and you could owe the remaining balance.
Before accepting help, ask what happens if your plans change. The money may still be worth it, but make sure today’s help won’t box you in tomorrow — especially when today’s mortgage rates are high enough that you might want to refinance later.
Spot the trade-offs and hidden costs
Using homebuying assistance might limit your ability to shop around. Government-backed programs can require you to select from a list of participating mortgage lenders. Unsurprisingly, grants given directly through a bank or mortgage company typically require you to get your mortgage there, too.
Some lenders offset the cost of homebuying assistance by charging you a higher interest rate, but the trade-off may be worth it if it helps you buy sooner. To compare total costs, get a Loan Estimate from at least three participating lenders offering assistance — plus a couple “regular” outside offers — to see which mortgage costs less overall.
If lender shopping stresses you out, a mortgage broker can help. Brokers compare rates and fees through a behind-the-scenes network of wholesale lenders — kind of like a travel agent comparing flights on your behalf. I learned an interesting tidbit when talking with a loan officer recently: Some wholesale lenders may offer assistance programs they don’t advertise directly to consumers, but a broker would know where to look.
Choose a lender with a proven track record of navigating down payment assistance. Throughout the homebuying process, your lender will work closely with the program to make sure the funds arrive on time to close.
Finally, ask a tax advisor about any tax implications, too. Depending on the program, you could receive a Form 1099-MISC and need to report the assistance as income.
Can assistance programs fix the affordability crisis?
Homebuying assistance can help buyers clear one hurdle, but it’s a long race. There’s a reason many assistance programs require you to complete a home buyer education course. The costs of homeownership are ongoing, including surprises like home repairs.
“Just throwing money at somebody doesn't solve the ultimate problem of affordability,” says Cheri Salazar, CEO of NestSTEPS, an employer-sponsored homeownership benefits and education platform.
Salazar, who co-founded NestSTEPS in January 2025, is betting on the next wave of homebuying assistance showing up in your employee benefits, alongside health insurance and retirement planning. Employer-backed homebuying programs are still niche, but some companies — usually large employers — see them as a tool for building worker loyalty and retention.
Earlier this year, financial services company BNY announced that eligible employees making $100,000 per year or less could qualify for $6,500 in down payment assistance toward the cost of their first home.
“This is something that the government has been trying and failing to accomplish for decades,” Salazar says. “And we believe that the real solution needs to come through the private sector.”

Title: NFL Week 2 Capsules
Article_Text:
Field Level Media
                
19 Sep 2026, 04:25 GMT+10
            
(Photo credit: Jim Dedmon)
Carolina Panthers (0-1) at Atlanta Falcons (0-1)
Sunday, 1:00 PM ET
FanDuel odds: Panthers -2.5, total 43.5
Series History: The Falcons lead the all-time series (37-25), but the Panthers have won four of the past five.
Carolina's offense exploded for 478 yards in Week 1 behind Bryce Young's 361 yards and three touchdowns passing, but turnovers and defensive breakdowns doomed the Panthers in a 59-37 loss to the Bears. Young has historically played well against Atlanta. WRs Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker and RB Chuba Hubbard give them multiple explosive options. Falcons RB Bijan Robinson has to be salivating after the Panthers allowed 291 rushing yards to the Bears. However, Atlanta didn't make a call at quarterback. It's likely Cooper Rush will make another start with Michael Penix Jr. (knee) possibly planning to return Thursday at Lambeau Field in Green Bay. Robinson, who posted 173 scrimmage yards in Week 1, has four consecutive games against Carolina with 100-plus yards from scrimmage. Atlanta struggled offensively in its loss to Pittsburgh, managing just 13 points and 238 total yards. Rush was particularly ineffective on third down, converting only 16.7% to first downs. Za'Darius Smith's two sacks and a strong secondary featuring A.J. Terrell and rookie Xavier Watts helped the Falcons stick around.
New Orleans Saints (0-1) at Baltimore Ravens (1-0)
FanDuel odds: Ravens -8.5, total 46.5
Series History: The Ravens have won four of the past five meetings.
The Saints went for two and the upset victory of Detroit in overtime in a one-point loss, but their offense came away looking like a winner. QB Tyler Shough's 410-yard, three-touchdown performance generated plenty of excitement around the young quarterback. WR Chris Olave had 182 receiving yards and New Orleans held up reasonably well in pass protection but did allow five sacks. Still, Shough was able to take consistent shots downfield. The Ravens overwhelmed Indianapolis in Week 1, generating turnovers and consistent pressure on Daniel Jones. Baltimore also put on an offensive show at Indy. QB Lamar Jackson appeared to have quickly mastered new play-caller Declan Doyle's scheme. Jackson threw for 324 yards and added a rushing touchdown, while Derrick Henry delivered a vintage performance with 144 rushing yards and three scores. Where Jackson will go with the ball on pass plays will depend on whether WR Zay Flowers (hamstring) is back in the lineup. Flowers posted a career-high 150 yards in Week 1 without playing a snap in the second half.
Minnesota Vikings (1-0) at Chicago Bears (1-0)
FanDuel odds: Bears -4.5, total 47.5
Series History: In the 2020s, the Vikings are 9-3 in this matchup. They swept the season series in 2021, 2022 and 2024.
Rain and wind could become a factor Sunday as the Vikings venture outside the dome for a second consecutive division matchup. Minnesota opened the season with a 39-22 win over Green Bay despite losing Kyler Murray (concussion) in the first half. Carson Wentz led the rally with four consecutive TD drives in the second half. Wentz had three touchdown passes and leaned heavily on WR Justin Jefferson, who finished with 92 yards and two scores. The Vikings did allow nearly 400 passing yards as they lived and died with the blitz, firing five-plus defenders into the pocket on more than 65 percent of their snaps. There will be a risk-reward balance at Chicago. The Bears put up 59 points with a dominant ground game producing six touchdowns. QB Caleb Williams said he's looking forward to the cat-and-mouse game with Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores. Williams had 269 yards and two touchdowns through the air and added two rushing TDs. D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai combined for 224 rushing yards. The Bears did not throw a perfect game defensively at Carolina and getting pressure on Wentz will be of significant importance.
Cincinnati Bengals (1-0) at Houston Texans (0-1)
FanDuel odds: Texans -2.5, total 45.5
Series History: The Texans have won four of the past five meetings.
Joe Burrow completed 71% of his passes and the Bengals generated 351 total yards against the Buccaneers, but they had their defense -- and three forced fumbles -- to thank for coming out on top. The Bengals had four sacks and four takeaways. They shift their focus to C.J. Stroud, who won't have No. 1 WR Nico Collins (hamstring) available. Stroud threw for 274 yards and two touchdowns in Week 1 while RB David Montgomery carried the offense with three TDs. The Texans can get to Burrow, but the issue last week was communication in the back seven. Houston was hammered by Josh Allen and the Bills for 409 total yards. With Collins out, the Bengals can tip the scales in their favor by handling Montgomery.
Pittsburgh Steelers (1-0) at New England Patriots (0-1)
FanDuel odds: Patriots -4.5, total 41.5
Series History: The Steelers lead 16-15; the Patriots have won three of the last four.
The Steelers let their defense do the dirty work in Week 1. LBs T.J. Watt and Alex Highsmith combined for four sacks, Watt had a pick-6 and the Falcons leaned almost entirely on RB Bijan Robinson for offense. The Patriots welcome back RB TreVeyon Henderson after he sat out Week 1 with an ankle injury. He brings a valuable speed and big-play threat, and QB Drake Maye could use a crutch after his three-INT opener at Seattle. Maye also lost No. 1 WR A.J. Brown (ankle) in the loss and Romeo Doubs didn't make a great first impression with costly drops. Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers (221 yards, one passing TD), back in Mike McCarthy's scheme, worked from the middle of the field to the sideline last week.
Green Bay Packers (0-1) at New York Jets (1-0)
FanDuel odds: Packers -3.5, total 44.5
Series History: The Packers have won three of the past four meetings.
There could be changes afoot on the Packers' offensive line. QB Jordan Love threw for 387 yards in a loss to the Vikings but felt pressure consistently. It might be too soon for major changes on defense, but coordinator Jonathon Gannon admitted this week Green Bay won't win games surrendering 39 points. WR Christian Watson looked the part as Love's go-to guy. He worked in the slot often, where his size and speed make him a nightmare for most defenses. Watson finished with 147 yards and two touchdowns. Second-year pro Matthew Golden added 95 receiving yards. The Packers are still searching for a rotation they can trust at running back with Josh Jacobs on the exempt list. The Jets opened their season with a convincing 23-10 win over Tennessee, highlighted by a balanced offensive attack and strong defensive play. Geno Smith was aggressive and efficient, completing nearly 80% of his passes. RB Breece Hall likely has Gannon concerned after he dominated with 118 total yards.
Cleveland Browns (0-1) at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (0-1)
FanDuel odds: Buccaneers -8.5, total 41.5
Series History: The Browns won the last meeting between these teams and hold a 7-4 advantage all-time.
Baker Mayfield gets a chance to show the Browns what they're missing after choosing Deshaun Watson over the former No. 1 pick in 2022. Mayfield, who bounced from Carolina to the Rams and then signed with the Buccaneers, said in the offseason this was a game he circled on his calendar. Watson kept the starting job after the Browns fell behind 31-0 at Jacksonville and lost 34-10. Rookie WR Denzel Boston caught a 59-yard touchdown in garbage time, the only highlight in a miserable offensive outing. The Browns struggled to protect Watson, who was sacked five times, lost a fumble and was intercepted. The Buccaneers lost three fumbles, and the costly mistakes tipped the scales in a Week 1 shootout loss to Cincinnati. Mayfield completed 82% of his passes and added a rushing touchdown. RB Bucky Irving contributed 93 scrimmage yards, and WR Emeka Egbuka (five catches, 63 yards) showed strong chemistry with Mayfield. The Browns had little choice but to abandon the running game and Quinshon Judkins. To keep this one tight, they'll need to generate longer drives and keep the vengeful Mayfield on the sideline.
Philadelphia Eagles (1-0) at Tennessee Titans (0-1)
FanDuel odds: Eagles -7, total 39.5
Series History: The Eagles lead the all-time series 8-5.
He heard some boos and then generated the opposite in the opener, but Jalen Hurts threw three touchdowns against the Commanders. RB Saquon Barkley rushed for 83 yards and TE Dallas Goedert delivered two touchdowns as the Eagles kept Washington's defense guessing. The Titans have a few riddles of their own to solve. They lost to the Jets in Week 1 and managed only 195 total yards. Cam Ward averaged only 4.4 yards per pass attempt which clogged lanes near the line of scrimmage in Brian Daboll's first game as offensive coordinator. On the defensive side, Titans LB Anthony Hill was exceptional, posting 16 tackles and two pass breakups. Ward will be responsible for creating big plays to keep pace with Philadelphia. If the Titans can slow Barkley and force Hurts to throw early and often, Tennessee can keep it tight.
Jacksonville Jaguars (1-0) at Denver Broncos (0-1)
Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET
FanDuel odds: Broncos -2.5, total 45.5
Series History: The home team has won four of the past five games in the series, which is tied 7-7 all-time.Jacksonville prepped for a rematch with the Broncos by destroying the Browns 34-10 last week. The Jaguars travel west to face the Broncos in Denver on Sunday. Bo Nix completed 17 of 28 passes for 131 yards, his lowest total since his rookie season in 2024. It certainly didn't help the third-year QB that he was sacked four times and hurried five more times, contributing to converting just 2 of 12 third downs. The Jaguars led the Browns 31-0 after the first drive of the second half before taking their foot off the gas. Trevor Lawrence, who found restored success last season under head coach Liam Coen, had nearly as many touchdown passes (four) as incompletions (five). Lawrence knows it will be tough to find the same success against a Denver defense that finished last season second in yards allowed (278.2 per game) and third in points allowed (18.3). While Denver led the league in sacks (68) a season ago, it managed just two in its loss at Kansas City, while Jacksonville's defense is tied for the league lead with five. That included 1.5 sacks apiece from former first-round picks Travon Walker and Josh Hines-Allen. The Jaguars' receiver room has bumps and bruises. Jacksonville removed Jakobi Meyers (thumb) and Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) from the injury report after they were limited throughout the week in practice.
Las Vegas Raiders (1-0) at Los Angeles Chargers (0-1)
Sunday, 4:05 PM ET
